notes: The verse's two supplied prepositions divide on rule 33's own test. The *with* of *filleth thee with the finest* answers to the English predicate's valency — *fill X with Y* is the only way English writes it — so it joins the verb's unit under rule 44. The *in* of *in thy borders* is a locative adjunct beside a verb whose English object is already *peace*, so it states what the bare nominal contributes and stays with `גְּבוּל`, though `גְּבוּלֵךְ` is what `שָׂם` governs in the Hebrew; the competing reading gives it to the verb under rule 33's direct-object deferral.
Both marginal glosses (*thy border peace*, *fat of wheat*) were read and set aside, by rule 38.
